doc.title: Vi Redd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999

title: Closing remarks and Mary Lou Williams
summary: Thanks, her sense of blessing, a mention of Mary Lou Williams and plans for a Part 2.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Well I want to thank you for sharing your time with me today.

Oh it’s been a pleasure. I think well, you know there are not too many of us around that were active in the 50s and 60s and 70s, and in sound mind and body. And I consider it a blessing that I’m still here to talk about things that have happened in the past and were very significant in terms of jazz history, and in terms of the roles of women in that. Oh we didn’t mention Mary Lou Williams. © Fillius Jazz Archive -20-
Well how could we — wasn’t she an unbelievable talent?

She used to write to me when she became so ill that she was down at Duke University, she used to write to me, and I’d write to her, at the time she was quite ill. But I’ll have to come back another time.
Yes. All right. Well thanks for your time.
